scope: Round 18: RAG training log. Save the RAG chat bot's conversations (visitor question, bot answer, retrieved knowledge chunks, guard outcome, feedback) so they can be reviewed and exported later to train the RAG system. Schema proposal: rag_sessions, rag_turns, rag_retrievals, rag_examples (see the schema discussion in this round). Flask (be/rag) never opens the database: every write goes through the Node API under /api/rag, as the existing functions do. One feature per function, id rag-train-<n>. Standing SRS rules: tests in the e2e folder, changed files described in docs/, all delete means soft delete.

features.title: Record each chat turn
features.user_visible_behavior: No visible change. Every answered, refused, handed-off or failed chat turn is saved with its outcome, model, prompt version, token counts and latency.
verification: Add POST /api/rag/turns in be/src/routes/rag.ts behind the internal token; Flask calls it through call_api from a new function file in be/rag/functions/ (one public function per file).
Store the visitor token as a sha256 hash in rag_sessions.visitor_hash; the raw token is never written.
Send a question as a guest and as a logged-in customer; one rag_sessions row and one rag_turns row per turn, with the right user_id (null for guests).
Send a prompt-injection test message; the row has outcome refused and guard_triggered set.
e2e spec in e2e/ checks the saved row after a chat request.
Logging failure does not break the chat reply: the visitor still gets the answer when the write fails.

features.title: Record retrieved chunks and citations
features.user_visible_behavior: No visible change. Each turn keeps the knowledge chunks the retriever returned, their rank and score, and whether the bot cited them.
verification: The retrieve step returns chunk ids, rank and score; the turn write sends them to POST /api/rag/turns.
cited is true only for chunks whose citation marker appears in the saved bot reply.
Deleting a knowledge document (soft delete) keeps its past rag_retrievals rows readable.
Unit test for the citation matcher in be/rag (pytest) and an e2e check of one saved turn with two chunks.

features.title: Thumbs up or down on a bot answer
features.user_visible_behavior: A visitor can tap thumbs up or thumbs down under a bot answer, and the choice stays after reload.
verification: Each bot bubble shows thumbs up and thumbs down buttons with accessible labels, at least 44px touch targets.
Tap thumbs down; rag_turns.feedback becomes down. Tapping the other button replaces it.
A visitor cannot set feedback on another visitor's turn (returns 403).
e2e spec covers tap, replace and reload.

features.title: Logging notice and opt-out
features.user_visible_behavior: The chat box tells visitors their messages are saved to improve the bot, and a visitor can opt out so their chats are not saved.
verification: Add a logging_consent column to rag_sessions (default true); migration applied.
The chat box shows a one-line notice with a link to the privacy text.
A visitor who opts out gets a session with logging_consent false and no rag_turns rows are written for it.
e2e spec: opt out, send a message, confirm no turn row is written.
docs/rag-training-log.md describes what is stored and the opt-out.

features.title: Staff review queue for saved turns
features.user_visible_behavior: Staff with the rag.review permission can list saved turns, label each one good, bad or needs fix, write a better reply, and approve or reject it.
verification: Add the rag.review permission to the Permission table and the seed; the admin role gets it.
GET /api/rag/review lists raw turns with their feedback and retrieved chunks; a customer without the permission gets 403.
Approving a turn creates one rag_examples row with status approved, label and ideal_reply; rejecting sets status rejected.
Turns already reviewed are not listed again by default.
e2e spec covers approve, reject and the 403 case.

features.title: Export approved examples for training
features.user_visible_behavior: Staff can download approved examples as a JSONL file, and each exported example is marked exported.
verification: GET /api/rag/examples/export (rag.review permission) returns JSONL with question, retrieved chunk texts, bot reply, ideal reply and label.
The file contains no user_id, visitor_hash, email or name.
Only status approved rows are included; after export they are marked exported with exported_at set.
Running the export twice does not duplicate rows.
Unit test for the field stripping and an e2e check of the download.

features.title: Soft-delete old unreviewed turns
features.user_visible_behavior: No visible change. Turns older than the retention period that were never reviewed are soft-deleted by a background job.
verification: Add RAG_TURN_RETENTION_DAYS to config (default 180); the job uses the existing job pattern and interval setting.
A turn older than the retention period with no rag_examples row gets deleted_at set; reviewed turns are kept.
Soft-deleted turns are excluded from the review queue and the export.
Unit test for the cutoff date and an e2e or API check of one run.
